correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md proof expands the difference of two independent Dirichlet(1,1,1) barycentric vectors with factorial moments, giving M1=e1/18, M2=(e1²−2e2)/60, M3=(23e1³−62e1e2+20e3)/4200. Independent exact rational expansion of all three polynomial moments agrees. Heron gives the sharp first-two bounds (9/5)M1²≤M2<(27/10)M1²; for fixed sum and sum of squares the positive triples lie on a full circle, and Lagrange multipliers force extrema of e3 to have two equal coordinates. The cubic inverse recovers all unordered squared sides for every nondegenerate triangle, with equilateral degeneracy handled by r=0.
residual_risks: Computations independently rederive k≤3 polynomials, not a general statistical stability theorem; claimed endpoint is exact algebra and geometry rather than sampling.
